00:00 Jordan: okay folks, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll run through the agenda quickly. We, uh we want to make sure we cover VPC wiring, SSO/KMS touches, pilot success criteria and a quick timeline. Samira gonna start?
00:28 Samira: yeah hi everyone, thanks — excited. Quick intro, I'm Samira, I'll be your CSM, main point of contact for go-live runbook and ops cadence.
00:40 Priya: hi thanks, Priya here. We're looking to get a private deployment, need the data to stay in our AWS account, and we have strict HIPAA-ish constraints.
00:55 Liam: hi, Liam, infra. We need to understand networking ports, egress, and the VPC peering or transit setup. Also curious about KMS integration for key material.
01:10 Ethan: great — quick heads up, our Redwood Private package is what most people pick here; we support VPC peering, and there's an option for customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll share specifics.
01:30 Marcus: security — we'll need to see SOC 2 docs, encryption at rest and in transit, and audit log retention details. There's also questions about RBAC and SSO.
01:45 Jordan: noted, Samira will own the SOC2 artifacts; Ethan will own the technical runbook + wiring. We'll also show a sample rollout plan for pilot -> ramp.
02:10 Samira: just to set expectations: typical timeline from ignition to pilot is 4-6 weeks depending on customer's security review and test dataset availability. That includes access, networking, a small throughput run, and then staging validation.
02:35 Sofia: can you clarify what "throughput run" means? We care about 95th percentile latency under load.
02:50 Ethan: yeah good question, by throughput run we mean a bench that simulates your QPS with representative sequences; we'll run our benchmark harness which measures tokens/sec, 95/99 p99 latency, and GPU utilization. We'll provide the harness and instructions.
03:15 Liam: which models are you planning to serve? We want to know cost implications, quantization options, and whether we can fall back to a smaller model if capacity's constrained.
03:33 Jordan: we can serve a curated open model from our catalog or customers can bring their own. For cost/latency tradeoffs we recommend a quantized variant for production - our Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest profiles.
03:50 Priya: okay, and about data residency — must remain in our VPC and logs only to our audit store. Can Redwood write logs anywhere else?
04:05 Samira: for Private deployments we can keep logs in customer's account; we support pushing audit logs to your S3 bucket and can configure Kafka or CloudWatch. We'll note that in the runbook.
04:30 Marcus: what's the default retention? We typically need 365 days. Also who has access to decrypted logs?
04:40 Samira: default is 90 days but we support custom retention; decrypted access is tenant-admin only. We'll document roles and RBAC mappings.
05:00 Ethan: technical note — our runtime manages KV cache and prefix caching to speed up repeated chat sessions. Apologies if the auto-transcript says K-V cash sometimes, it's K-V cache.
05:18 Priya: heh yeah that earlier transcript noise. Can you explain the KV cache so our developers understand?
05:25 Ethan: sure, simplified: the KV cache stores attention state between generation steps so repeated prefixes don't need recomputing; it reduces per-token compute and improves latency. In our bench you'll see big gains for session-based workloads.
05:50 Jordan: demo plan: after wiring is in place we'll do a smoke test, then run a 1-hour throughput test, then a 2-week pilot against a small set of users.
06:05 Sofia: what's the SLO you can commit to during pilot?
06:10 Jordan: for Dedicated/private we target 95th < 300ms for short responses under typical QPS; actual SLO depends on sequence length and model. We'll capture target numbers in the SLA section of the runbook.
06:30 Liam: how do we handle failover? If a node saturates, do you auto-fallback to a cheaper model or queue requests?
06:42 Ethan: we have smart routing policies; we can route by latency or cost tiers and fall back to smaller model variants automatically. We also support canary rollouts for model versions.
07:10 Priya: for our pilot success criteria we want: (1) 95th latency < 500ms for typical payloads, (2) accuracy regression within 2% of baseline human evals, (3) zero data exfiltration incidents.
07:30 Jordan: good, we'll capture those as pilot KPIs. We'll also run a couple of example eval sets to measure quality regressions — can you share representative prompts?
07:50 Sofia: yes, we can share a redacted dataset of 2k prompts. Internal legal will sign off; we'll share by next Monday.
08:05 Marcus: legal will also need proof of encryption and key lifecycle management — how are keys handled?
08:20 Ethan: option A: Redwood-managed KMS (we store keys in our KMS), option B: customer-managed KMS/HSM in your account where we never touch the keys. For highest assurance pick B. We can walk through the KMS policies.
08:50 Jordan: noted — we'll add KMS integration steps to the wiring doc and include IAM policy snippets.
09:05 Samira: small admin note — our console gives token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. During pilot we'll give you RBAC to the console for telemetry.
09:25 Liam: ok great — what's the mechanism for pushing logs to our SIEM?
09:35 Ethan: we can stream audit logs via Kinesis/CloudWatch to your SIEM, or drop daily exports to S3 encrypted with your key.
09:48 Marcus: good. Also need to confirm penetration test windows and support for compliance scans.
09:55 Samira: we schedule a compliance window; we can support scans with agreed scope and notify our security team. We'll include the schedule template.
10:20 Jordan: switching to rollout timeline: ignition (week 0) - wiring and access; week 1 - smoke and small bench; week 2 - scaled bench and validation; week 3-4 pilot; week 5 ramp to production. Typical 4-6 week runway.
10:42 Priya: do you have a suggested staff plan? We'll need a primary Redwood on-call and a SE, plus our dev and infra folks for cutover.
10:55 Jordan: yes, recommended staffing: CSM + SE for first 4 weeks, then a recurring operational sync weekly. We'll set on-call rotation for incidents.
11:15 Sofia: one thing — rate-limiting. We want to protect our backend during spikes. How is throttling handled?
11:25 Ethan: Redwood supports per-API key quotas and token-based rate limits; we can configure hard caps on concurrency and burst allowances. We'll document config knobs in the runbook.
11:48 Liam: earlier you mentioned batching. For us batch sizes might vary, how does batching affect latency?
12:00 Ethan: batching increases throughput and reduces cost per token but can add latency. We have workload-aware batching and dynamic thresholds tuned to meet latency SLOs; we'll show sample configs after the bench.
12:25 Priya: let's talk about the bench — what do you need from us?
12:30 Ethan: sample payloads (json), expected concurrency pattern (p50/p95/p99 qps), and a set of sequence lengths. If you can give 1 hour of production traces that's ideal.
12:55 Jordan: action recap: Jordan sends wiring doc; Samira SOC2; Ethan bench harness; customer sends dataset and traffic profile.
13:10 Marcus: we also need to validate access control — who can rotate keys, who can view logs in decrypted form.
13:20 Samira: we'll provide a role matrix template for you to review.
13:35 Priya: any gotchas for VPC connectivity? Things like ephemeral public egress IPs, or certain ports?
13:45 Ethan: yes, if you want strict egress only to your logging endpoints we'll set NAT egress to your egress nat gateway; ports primarily 443 outbound and some internal health ports for infra. We'll share a minimal firewall policy.
14:05 Liam: are there data transfer costs? This is an on-prem-ish private deployment inside our cloud but curious about egress billing and token costs.
14:20 Jordan: token costs are usage-based; for Private deployments cost structure is a combination of reserved capacity + usage. We'll put a draft pricing sheet in the follow-up. Data transfer within same region usually minimal but cross-region egress is billed by cloud vendor.
14:45 Sofia: ok good.
15:00 Jordan: any other immediate blockers?
15:05 Priya: legal review timelines — we might take two weeks; that could extend the ignition.
15:15 Samira: we can parallelize benching and wiring while legal reviews docs to shorten calendar.
15:30 Liam: timeline looks good. When can we do the deep technical bench?
15:35 Ethan: propose week of 2026-08-10; I'll send an invite to Liam and Sofia.
15:45 Jordan: I'll try to get wiring doc out by Friday 2026-08-06. Samira will post SOC2 artifacts to your S3 share.
16:00 Priya: perfect, thanks everyone. Quick recap?
16:05 Jordan: recap: (1) Jordan sends wiring doc & CF templates; (2) Samira uploads SOC2 and SSO notes; (3) Ethan runs bench and schedules deep dive with Liam; (4) Kepler shares dataset and traffic profile. Next call target: bench deep-dive 2026-08-11.
16:30 End of meeting.
